outlook.body:
- Balance Upstream and Downstream aluminium businesses as the core operating strategy, complemented by Copper and Specialty Alumina

- Strengthen upstream cost advantage against global peers by operationalising captive coal mines and reducing cost of production
- Build a digital-first culture using enterprise data platforms, industrial IoT, AI/ML models, digital twins, and next-generation conversation-based Gen AI
- Advance a long-horizon sustainability roadmap covering renewable energy, water stewardship, circularity/waste-to-value, and biodiversity, retaining leadership in the S&P Global CSA
- Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (approved 13-Feb-2017, amended 22-Feb-2021, reviewed 13-Feb-2024) under SEBI LODR. The Board endeavours to distribute dividend in the range of 8% to 10% of Free Cash Flow at Hindalco consolidated level, where Free Cash Flow is defined as cash flow after meeting interest, tax, other statutory dues, maintenance capital expenditure and working capital requirements, but before strategic capital expenditure and debt repayments/pre-payments. Dividend recommendations weigh free cash flow, stability of earnings, future capex and inorganic growth/reinvestment opportunities, industry outlook and stage of business cycle, leverage profile and capital adequacy, economic/regulatory environment, contingent liabilities, past dividend trends and possible buyback. Policy is reviewed/amended periodically.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Hindalco is advancing a long-term growth agenda that expands upstream Aluminium and Copper capacities while accelerating value-added downstream, alongside its wholly owned subsidiary Novelis. In Aluminium Upstream, a 374 KT brownfield expansion at the Aditya smelter and an 850 KT greenfield alumina refinery at Kansariguda are progressing well and are expected to keep Hindalco in the first quartile of the global cost curve, supported by captive coal and bauxite. In Aluminium Downstream, the Company commissioned a 170 KT FRP facility at Aditya during FY 2025-26 and enhanced capacity across battery enclosures, battery foils, AC fins, aerospace-grade alloys, and packaging foils, targeting a fourfold increase in India downstream EBITDA by FY 2029-30 (from FY 2023-24 levels). Specialty Alumina, among the global top three producers, remains on track to scale to ~1 MTPA by FY 2029-30 across flame retardants, ceramics, catalysts, white fused alumina, and precipitated hydrates. In Copper, Hindalco is commissioning a 300 KT smelter expansion, adding 25 KT of inner grooved tubes, and entering copper and multi-metal e-waste recycling to capture air-conditioning and electrification demand. Novelis is executing a multi-year organic growth programme: it is on track to commission the ~$5 billion, 600 KT integrated Bay Minette (U.S.) rolling and recycling facility in FY 2026-27 (~two-thirds dedicated to beverage packaging), is pursuing debottlenecking and recycling expansions at Guthrie (U.S.), UAL (South Korea), Pindamonhangaba (Brazil) and Logan (U.S.), and targeted recycling/rolling capacity expansions at Latchford (UK) and Oswego (U.S.), the latter delayed by fire incidents in FY 2025-26; the Oswego hot mill resumed operations in June 2026. Novelis is also evaluating further capacity additions in supply-constrained regions and continues its 3x30 sustainability and circularity vision.

outlook.body:
- Indian aluminium demand expected to keep growing above GDP on broad-based sectoral momentum (electrical, automotive, infrastructure), though rising imports of rolled and foil products from China and FTA countries remain a key concern, partly countered by government anti-dumping duties
- Global primary aluminium demand expected to grow ~1% to ~75 Mt in CY2026 with the market shifting into a deficit of ~1.5 Mt, supporting firm prices
- Domestic refined copper demand expected to grow ~6-7% in FY2026-27, reaching ~1 Mn tons, with copper prices supported by trade tensions and sharply lower TC/RCs reflecting tight concentrate supply
- Novelis sees strong long-term demand for aluminium rolled products driven by economic growth, material substitution, and sustainability (shift away from PET plastics toward infinitely recyclable aluminium beverage packaging)
- Automotive aluminium sheet demand to grow on lightweighting benefits (lower emissions, better fuel economy) and the rise of EVs where lighter weight extends battery range
- Aerospace plate and sheet demand favourable on strong OEM build rates and significant Airbus/Boeing order backlogs, though constrained near-term by OEM supply-chain instability
- Novelis EBITDA-per-tonne recovery to the >$600/tonne long-term target supported by the Bay Minette expansion, the global cost-efficiency programme, and improved scrap pricing/availability as China competition subsides
- Oswego plant fires and tariff headwinds temporarily impacted Novelis volumes and profitability in FY2025-26, with tariff impact expected to be largely mitigated by securing additional U.S. cold-rolling capacity
- Novelis' multi-year supply agreements position it to benefit from future aerospace demand as significant aircraft-industry order backlogs for key OEMs including Airbus and Boeing translate into future growth

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Hindalco operates across the full aluminium value chain in India—from bauxite mining, alumina refining, coal mining and captive power to aluminium smelting and downstream rolling, extruding and foil making—alongside a copper business built around a custom copper smelter and a specialty alumina business. demand_drivers.body:

- Novelis sees strong long-term demand for aluminium rolled products driven by economic growth, material substitution, and sustainability (shift away from PET plastics toward infinitely recyclable aluminium beverage packaging)
- Automotive aluminium sheet demand to grow on lightweighting benefits (lower emissions, better fuel economy) and the rise of EVs where lighter weight extends battery range
- Aerospace plate and sheet demand favourable on strong OEM build rates and significant Airbus/Boeing order backlogs, though constrained near-term by OEM supply-chain instability
- Novelis EBITDA-per-tonne recovery to the >$600/tonne long-term target supported by the Bay Minette expansion, the global cost-efficiency programme, and improved scrap pricing/availability as China competition subsides
- Oswego plant fires and tariff headwinds temporarily impacted Novelis volumes and profitability in FY2025-26, with tariff impact expected to be largely mitigated by securing additional U.S. cold-rolling capacity
- Novelis' multi-year supply agreements position it to benefit from future aerospace demand as significant aircraft-industry order backlogs for key OEMs including Airbus and Boeing translate into future growth
